_readme: Nordic and Baltic university directory. Every fact comes from the official national portal or ministry listed in each country's "sources". Update "checked" when you re-verify a country. Ownership is null when no official source states it.

countries.name: Sweden
countries.scope: Every university and university college that admits students through University Admissions in Sweden (40 institutions).
countries.ownershipNote: Public = state higher education institution; private = independent education provider, as classified by the Swedish Higher Education Authority (UKÄ).

rules.applicationFee: SEK 900 per semester for citizens of countries outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland. One fee covers all the programmes you choose in that round. Doctoral applicants pay no fee.
rules.tuition: Citizens of countries outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland pay tuition for bachelor’s and master’s studies. Each university sets its own amount — it is shown in the search results on University Admissions and on the university’s website. Doctoral studies are free of tuition fees.
rules.english: English 6: IELTS Academic 6.5 with no section below 5.5 · TOEFL iBT 4.5 on the new 1–6 scale (no section below 4) or 90 with writing 20 on the old scale · Cambridge C1 Advanced 180 · PTE Academic 62 (writing 61). Some degrees taught in English count instead of a test — see the official page.
entry: Bachelor’s: completed upper secondary (high school) education, English 6 and Mathematics 1a, 1b or 1c, plus any specific requirements of the programme.
Master’s: a bachelor’s degree equivalent to a Swedish kandidatexamen, English 6 and the programme’s specific requirements.

scholarships.label: Swedish Institute Scholarships for Global Professionals

rules.scholarshipNote: Many universities also offer tuition-fee scholarships to fee-paying students — see each university’s website.

countries.name: Finland
countries.scope: All 13 universities and 22 universities of applied sciences listed by Study in Finland.
countries.ownershipNote: All are publicly funded: universities are public-law corporations or foundations funded by the State, and universities of applied sciences are public limited companies in the Ministry of Education and Culture’s branch.

rules.applicationFee: €100 for applicants from outside the EU/EEA (Studyinfo application fee).
rules.tuition: Students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland usually pay tuition for English-taught bachelor’s and master’s programmes — typically €9,000 to €20,000 a year depending on the university and programme. Doctoral programmes are tuition-free. Universities often offer scholarships to fee-paying students.
rules.english: IELTS, TOEFL, PTE and Cambridge English are commonly accepted. Minimum scores are set by each university and programme.
entry: Bachelor’s: a school-leaving certificate that qualifies you for higher education in your home country. Some programmes add entrance exams, SAT or interviews.
Master’s: a bachelor’s degree. Master’s programmes at universities of applied sciences also require two years of relevant work experience.

deadlines.label: Joint application for autumn 2027 start opens
Joint application for autumn 2027 closes (15:00 Finnish time)

rules.deadlineNote: Some programmes run separate applications (mainly December–January) or rolling admission — check the programme on Studyinfo.fi.
rules.funds: Residence permit: at least €800 a month (€9,600 a year) — the minimum set by the Finnish Immigration Service.
rules.scholarshipNote: Scholarships for fee-paying students are offered by the universities themselves — see each university’s tuition-fee page.

countries.name: Norway
countries.scope: Every institution listed by Study in Norway (the Directorate for Higher Education and Skills): universities, specialised universities and university colleges.
countries.ownershipNote: Study in Norway and NOKUT group institutions by type, not by ownership, so we do not label them public or private here. Fees for non-EU students apply at public institutions too.

rules.applicationFee: Not specified by Study in Norway — check the institution’s admission page.
rules.tuition: Degree-seeking students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland must normally pay tuition fees. Amounts vary by institution and programme. Doctoral candidates and students on schemes such as NORPART, NORHED, Fulbright, Students at Risk and some Erasmus Mundus degrees are exempt.
rules.english: Document your English according to the institution’s requirements. Accepted tests and scores vary from institution to institution.
entry: Bachelor’s: the Higher Education Entrance Qualification — foreign qualifications are assessed against the official GSU list for your country. English-taught bachelor’s programmes admit through the institution’s own system.
Master’s: a recognised bachelor’s degree comparable to 180 ECTS, including at least 1½ years of full-time study in a relevant subject. Some programmes set a minimum grade average.
rules.deadlineNote: Each institution sets its own deadline for international applicants — see the institution’s admission page.
rules.funds: Residence permit: at least NOK 170,368 a year (NOK 15,488 a month) for 2026–2027, in addition to tuition.
rules.scholarshipNote: Some institutions, such as the University of Oslo, state that they offer no scholarships that cover tuition.

countries.name: Lithuania
countries.scope: Every university and college that lists English-taught programmes on Study in Lithuania (26 institutions).
countries.ownershipNote: Study in Lithuania does not say which institutions are state or private, so we only mark ownership where the institution’s official name says it is a state institution.

rules.applicationFee: Set by each university and programme.
rules.tuition: Study in Lithuania gives average fees of €2,000–€5,000 a year for bachelor’s and €3,000–€6,000 a year for master’s studies (FAQ last updated 2023). The exact fee is on each programme page.
rules.english: Set by each university and programme — see the programme’s “More information” page.
entry: Each university runs its own admission. Your documents go through recognition and subject-equivalence checks, which can take a month or longer — apply early.
rules.deadlineNote: Deadlines for the autumn semester at most universities are in June. Several universities also offer a spring intake.
rules.funds: Living costs: about €500–€800 a month depending on the city (Study in Lithuania).

countries.name: Latvia
countries.scope: Every institution featured on Study in Latvia (the State Education Development Agency), with the number of English-taught programmes it lists, plus the Latvian Academy of Music from the Ministry’s list.
countries.ownershipNote: Public = “State” and private = “Private”, as labelled by Study in Latvia.

portal.label: Apply directly to each university (often via DreamApply)

rules.applicationFee: A non-refundable application fee of around €150–€200.
rules.tuition: From under €1,600 a year for some bachelor’s programmes up to €25,600 for an Executive MBA. The fee for each programme is on Study in Latvia and the university’s website.
rules.english: English at CEFR level B2 or higher. How you prove it depends on the country where you studied.
entry: Bachelor’s: a secondary school certificate that allows you to enter the chosen studies.
Master’s: a bachelor’s degree in a relevant field. Your diploma is assessed by the Academic Information Centre (AIC).
rules.deadlineNote: Study in Latvia says non-EU applicants should apply by the beginning of June for the autumn semester and by mid-October or the beginning of November for spring. This guidance dates from 2021 — confirm the date with the university.
rules.funds: Living costs: about €450–€700 a month (Study in Latvia).

countries.name: Austria
countries.scope: Every higher education institution listed by Study in Austria (OeAD): 23 public universities, 21 universities of applied sciences, 19 private universities and 14 university colleges of teacher education.
countries.ownershipNote: Public = the “Universities” group and private = the “Private universities” group on Study in Austria. Universities of applied sciences and teacher-education colleges are not labelled by ownership there, except colleges whose official name says “Private”.

rules.applicationFee: Not specified by Study in Austria — check the institution.
rules.tuition: Public universities: non-EU students holding a student residence permit generally pay €726.72 per semester, plus the compulsory €26.20 students’ union (ÖH) fee. Universities of applied sciences and private universities set their own fees. Exemptions are possible for some scholarship holders, exchange students and students from specific countries.
rules.english: Most programmes are taught in German, with a growing number in English. The language requirement and accepted certificates are set by each programme.
entry: Bachelor’s: a secondary school leaving certificate that entitles you to university study in your home country, plus proof of the teaching language (German for German-taught programmes).
Master’s: a relevant bachelor’s degree of at least six semesters (180 ECTS). PhD: a master’s degree in a related field.
Foreign documents must be legalised; documents not in German or English need legalised translations. Some programmes (e.g. medicine, arts, many UAS programmes) have entrance exams.
rules.deadlineNote: These are the general deadlines Study in Austria gives for universities. Universities of the arts, private universities, universities of applied sciences and teacher-education colleges have their own deadlines, and programmes with entrance exams can close up to six months before the semester.

entry: Admission depends on the country where you earned your school certificate: swissuniversities publishes the requirement for each country and each university — for some countries this means one or two years of university study first, or a complementary exam (ECUS).

countries.scope: Every public, state and active private higher education institution on the Ministry of Education’s list of higher education institutions (archive edition — the Ministry is moving to a new website).
countries.ownershipNote: Public and state institutions are marked public; private institutions as private — as grouped by the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports.

portal.label: Study in Czechia — how to apply

rules.applicationFee: Most universities charge an application fee; the amount is set by each university.
rules.tuition: Degree programmes taught in Czech at public and state universities are tuition-free for all nationalities. English-taught programmes charge tuition set by each university.
rules.english: Set by each university and programme. Czech-taught programmes usually require Czech at level B2.
entry: Each university sets its own requirements, deadlines and process. Your previous education may need official recognition (nostrification) — start early.
Some programmes have entrance exams, interviews or portfolio reviews in spring or early summer.
rules.deadlineNote: Many applications for September start close between February and April; results are often announced in June–July. Always follow the deadline of your programme.

countries.name: Poland
countries.scope: The 112 universities supervised by the Ministry of Science and Higher Education that have a framework agreement with NAWA (Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange) for 2026/27.
countries.ownershipNote: The NAWA list does not say which universities are public or private, so ownership is not shown.

rules.tuition: About €1,000–6,000 a year for bachelor’s and €1,500–8,000 for master’s and long-cycle studies; medicine, dentistry and MBA programmes €12,000–15,000 or more. Doctoral schools are tuition-free and full-time candidates receive a scholarship. (NAWA, December 2023.)
rules.english: English-taught programmes require at least B2 — a certificate or previous education fully in English.
entry: There is no central application system — you apply to the university.
Foreign diplomas are recognised through international agreements or by nostrification at a Polish university; check with ENIC-NARIC Poland.
rules.deadlineNote: Admission campaigns usually start in April or May and can run for up to six months, depending on the university.
rules.funds: Living costs start from about €600 a month; the average student spends about €890 (NAWA).

countries.ownershipNote: The official list does not label institutions public, church or private, so ownership is not shown.

entry: Bachelor’s: a secondary school diploma and transcript (with Hungarian or English translation); some programmes have an entrance exam.
Master’s: a bachelor’s degree; PhD: a master’s-equivalent degree.
rules.deadlineNote: Self-financed applications: first round usually in November for February start; second round in February for September start; decisions around late July. Check the institution for exact dates.

countries.scope: Every institution with English-taught degree programmes listed by Study in Croatia, with each programme by level.
countries.ownershipNote: Study in Croatia does not label institutions public or private, so ownership is not shown.

portal.label: Study in Croatia — how to apply

rules.applicationFee: Possible application fees of €60–300, set by each institution.
rules.tuition: Per year for international students: humanities and social sciences €1,100–10,400; natural and technical sciences about €1,000–6,000; medical studies €10,000–12,000. Each institution sets its own fees.
rules.english: You need knowledge of English for English-taught programmes; the institution sets how you prove it.
entry: Undergraduate Croatian-taught programmes use the national “Postani student!” system; graduate programmes use diplomski.studij.hr or the institution; postgraduate programmes always apply to the institution. For English-taught programmes contact the institution directly.
Admission requirements (previous qualification, grades, special skills) are set by each institution.
rules.deadlineNote: Set by each institution — contact the institution for its calendar.
rules.funds: You must show enough money for your stay, from your own funds or a scholarship.
rules.scholarshipNote: Some institutions may offer partial tuition fee waivers.

countries.name: Germany
countries.scope: Every state-recognised higher education institution in the German Rectors’ Conference (HRK) Hochschulkompass list, except public-administration colleges that only train civil servants.
countries.ownershipNote: Public = public-law (state) institution; private = private, state-recognised institution, as recorded by the HRK. Church-run institutions are state-recognised but not labelled public or private.

portal.label: Apply via the university or uni-assist

rules.applicationFee: Universities that use uni-assist charge its handling fee: €75 for the first course of study and €30 for each additional one in the same semester. Direct applications are often free — check the university.
rules.tuition: Public universities generally charge no tuition for bachelor’s and most master’s programmes; you pay a semester contribution of about €70–430. Exceptions: Baden-Württemberg charges non-EU students €1,500 per semester, and institutions in Bavaria may charge non-EU/EEA students fees they set themselves. Private institutions charge their own fees.
rules.english: English-taught programmes need proof of English (accepted tests and scores are set by each programme) and no German. German-taught programmes usually require German at B2 or higher.
entry: Bachelor’s: your school certificate must be recognised as a higher education entrance qualification. If it is not, you need two or three semesters of comparable university study at home, or a foundation course (Studienkolleg) and its final exam.
Master’s: a recognised bachelor’s degree in a relevant subject; programmes set their own grade and subject requirements.
Applicants from outside the EU/EEA apply through uni-assist or directly to the university, as the university specifies.
rules.deadlineNote: Each university sets its own deadlines — check the programme in the DAAD International Programmes database or on the university’s website.
rules.funds: Student visa: proof of €992 a month for living costs (amount in force from 1 January 2025), usually through a blocked account.
